notes: All RNG-based tests seed np.random.default_rng() with a fixed integer seed -- deterministic, non-flaky.

Statistical/distributional claims (RoundErr~0.25, scaled-error-ratio~1/s) use large sample sizes (200,000) or many-trial Monte-Carlo aggregation (400 trials, aggregate not per-trial ratios) with loose tolerances (abs=0.01, rel=0.3) specifically to avoid flakiness while still being a meaningful check.

Optimization-improvement claims (GPTQ vs RTN, SmoothQuant migrated vs raw, AWQ alpha search) all assert a directional inequality (<=, <) rather than an exact match, appropriate for 'does the paper's method actually improve on the naive baseline' claims.

Identity/algebraic claims (SmoothQuant Eq.3 migration equivalence, uniform-quant Eq.1 scale formulas, GPTQ Eq.3 Hessian update) are checked to floating-point precision (atol 1e-6 to 1e-9) since these are exact mathematical identities in the papers, not approximations.
